title: Kesän puutarhaopastukset Kaisaniemessä
content:
On a guided tour, you’ll journey through millions of years of evolution along the paths of the Evolution Garden, and immerse yourself in a world of scents and colours in the Garden of the senses. You’ll also admire unique lichen and moss gardens, while hearing stories about the garden’s past and present, and the buildings found in the area.

Tours will take place from June 23 to August 22, 2026. Free entrance, no prior registration required.

  • Tuesdays, Fridays and Saturdays at 15 (3 pm)

    • The tour starts at the greenhouse entrance and lasts approximately 40 minutes.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Arkadiankadun siltaremontti aiheuttaa muutoksia liikennejärjestelyihin Luonnontieteellisen museon lähistöllä
content:
The renovation will start with the construction of temporary traffic arrangements from Wednesday 7 January onwards. The renovation is expected to be completed in late 2026.

A temporary bridge for pedestrians will be built on the east side of Arkadiankatu over the Baana. The aim is to maintain the pedestrian route on the east side of the bridge until the temporary bridge is operational. Cyclists will also be able to use the bridge.

The Baana route underneath the bridge is expected to remain open for most of the renovation's duration, with some minor exceptions.

There will be changes to the motor vehicle routes by the bridge and around it in January. If possible, should be favoured during the bridge renovation.

Connections to the bus terminals in Kamppi will remain available, but there will be a slight diversion of routes.

Trams 1 and 1T will run via Simonkatu and Kamppi. Lasipalatsi and the Natural History Museum will not be served.

The diversion is due to the renovation of the Arkadiankatu bridge and will remain in place until late 2026. The renovation will not affect HSL's bus services.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Terveet elintavat keski-iässä tuovat paitsi vuosia myös onnellisuutta vanhuuteen
content:
Helsingin yliopiston tutkijat seurasivat lähes 2 700 suomalaista miestä yli 50 vuoden ajan, aina elämän loppuun asti. Seuranta alkoi 1960- ja 1970-luvuilla, kun miehet olivat keskimäärin 42-vuotiaita ja terveitä.

University of Helsinki researchers followed almost 2,700 Finnish men for over 50 years, until the end of their lives. The monitoring began in the 1960s and 1970s, when the men were on average 42 years old and healthy.

The researchers measured five factors contributing to cardiovascular risk: smoking, body mass index, blood pressure, cholesterol and blood glucose. The better the values for each factor, the longer the men lived. 

Of the men with positive values for all five factors, 42% reached the age of 90. The corresponding figure for those with poor values for all five was 7%.

The study did not stop at measuring lifespan. In 2007, when the surviving research subjects averaged 79 years of age, they were asked about their functional capacity, happiness and quality of life.

title: Uudet HOB-kirjat käsittelevät veropolitiikkaa, monikriisiajan viestintää sekä tutkimuksen ja aktivismin suhteita
content:
The following open access books were published in  between April and August 2026:​​​​​​​

  • Laura Kolbe, Mikko Posti, Jussi Jännes & Meena Lindroos (toim.): (2026). This publication by Urbaria examines the street as a place, an experience and a subject of research from the perspectives of various academic disciplines, and explores its significance in the past, present and future of cities.
  • Henrietta Grönlund, Riikka Hohti, Paula Ahola & Nuusa Niskala (toim.): (2026). In this bilingual publication, activism is explored as a subject of research, as a critical dimension that enriches or challenges academic practice, and as a question relevant to researchers.
  • Esko Linnakangas: (2026). The book examines the impact of government programmes on tax regulation and discusses the characteristics of a sound tax policy.
  • Risto Koulu: (2026). The book analyses judicial practices relating to summary civil cases (relatively minor debt collection cases) from the perspectives of legal history, legal theory and empirical research, and proposes ways of improving the system.

title: New FIMM Group Leader Tuomo Hartonen explores the future of health foundation models
content:
Following an international group leader recruitment process in the field of data science and AI for molecular and health data, Hartonen was appointed to a FIMM-EMBL Group Leader position starting on 1 September.

Hartonen holds master's degrees in both theoretical physics and translational medicine and earned his PhD in medical genetics from the University of Helsinki. In June 2025, following his postdoctoral work at FIMM and a research visit at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg, he received the highly competitive Academy Research Fellowship from Research Council of Finland.

His currently brings together expertise ranging from neuroscience and statistics to machine learning and epidemiology, with additional recruitment planned in the coming months.

Hartonen's route to becoming a group leader has not been the most conventional one. Interested in understanding “how things work and why the world is how it is” from an early age, he initially considered both physics and history before choosing physics after a high school field trip to CERN.

title: Bernardo Williams väittelee aiheesta Geometriset menetelmät bayesilaisessa päättelyssä ja diskreetin datan mallinnuksessa
content:
M.Sc. Bernardo Williams defends his PhD thesis “Geometric Methods for Bayesian Inference and Modeling Discrete Data” on Friday the 18th of September 2026 at 13 in the University of Helsinki Physicum Building, Auditorium E204 (Gustaf Hällströmin katu 2, 2nd floor). His opponent is Assistant Professor Martin Trapp (KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden) and custos Professor Arto Klami (University of Helsinki). The defence will be held in English.

The thesis of Bernardo Williams is a part of research done in the Department of Computer Science and in the Multi-source Probabilistic Inference group at the University of Helsinki. His supervisors have been Professor Arto Klami and Academy Research Fellow Marcelo Hartmann (University of Helsinki).
